newsitem.title: UK: Decision on Ford action expected Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Decision on Ford action expected Thursday.

text.p: Workers at Ford Motor Co on Monday started a series of mass meetings around the country in protest over job cuts at the Halewood plant but a decision on whether to hold a strike ballot will not be made until Thursday, a union spokesman said.
Workers at some 20 plants will meet on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday and union leaders will report back to Ford management on Thursday at a previously scheduled meeting in London.
Ford confirmed the Thursday meeting with the unions.
Ford last week announced 1,300 job losses out of a workforce of around 4,500 at Halewood in Liverpool, northwest England, which produces Escort cars for the domestic market.
A spokesman for the Transport and General Workers Union (TGWU) said that Ford's National Joint Negotiating Committee would not make any decision until after the Thursday meeting with management.

"The mass meetings over the next few days are consultative. The National Joint Negotiating Committee will wait until Thursday to decide whether or not to hold a ballot on strike action," the spokesman told Reuters.
Under Britain's trade union laws, it could take two or three weeks to set up a secret ballot and get the results.
The unions believe Ford plans to build the next, updated version of the Escort at factories in Germany and Spain.
